services.desc: Tony and GRAMMY Award winner Ari’el Stachel takes the stage at Maine Jewish Museum in OTHER, his acclaimed autobiographical one-man show about what happens when the person the world sees and the person you know yourself to be don’t quite match. Stachel shot to Broadway prominence originating the role of Haled in The Band’s Visit, winning the 2018 Tony Award for Best Featured Actor in a Musical. But behind that extraordinary success was a far more complicated story. Growing up as the son of a Yemenite-Israeli father and an Ashkenazi-American mother in the post-9/11 United States, Stachel learned early how quickly other people could assign him an identity. services.desc: Ghanaian culture portrays portraiture as a meaningful way to honor subjects through a wide variety of media, reflecting the fluidity and movement of memory and history. With this exhibition, guest curator Myron M. Beasley introduces us to four contemporary artists from the Artemartis collective in Accra, each offering a snapshot of everyday life and the city’s social and cultural identity. This exhibition narrates a personal journey with a continued focus of the artist’s work on how the individual narrative anchors the collective, and vice versa. blurb: The museum resides within the restored Etz Chaim Synagogue, a turn-of-the-century house of worship. The museum hosts rotating eight-week art exhibitions featuring Jewish-connected and Maine-connected artists, as well as topical themes relevant to the Maine Jewish community.
